english: Let $C$ be the curve $y=x^{3}+3x^{2}+5x+8$. The normal to $C$ at its point of inflection is a normal to the parabola $y^{2}=16x$ at a point $P$, and it meets the parabola again at the point $Q$. If $O$ is the origin, then the area of the triangle $OPQ$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $C$ वक्र $y=x^{3}+3x^{2}+5x+8$ है। $C$ के नति परिवर्तन बिन्दु पर $C$ का अभिलम्ब, परवलय $y^{2}=16x$ के किसी बिन्दु $P$ पर अभिलम्ब है, तथा यह परवलय को पुनः बिन्दु $Q$ पर मिलता है। यदि $O$ मूलबिन्दु है, तो त्रिभुज $OPQ$ का क्षेत्रफल ______ है।
solution: Normal to $y^{2}=16x$ ($a=4$) at $t$: $y=-tx+8t+4t^{3}$; slope $-\dfrac{1}{2}\Rightarrow t=\dfrac{1}{2}$, intercept $4+\dfrac{1}{2}=\dfrac{9}{2}$ (matches); $P(1,4)$
solution_full: $y'=3x^{2}+6x+5$ and $y''=6x+6$. $y''$ changes sign at $x=-1$, so the point of inflection is $(-1,\,-1+3-5+8)=(-1,5)$, where $y'=3-6+5=2$.
The normal to $C$ there has slope $-\dfrac{1}{2}$: $y-5=-\dfrac{1}{2}(x+1)$, i.e. $y=-\dfrac{1}{2}x+\dfrac{9}{2}$, or $x+2y=9$.

For $y^{2}=16x$, $a=4$; the normal at $(4t^{2},8t)$ is $y=-tx+8t+4t^{3}$, with slope $-t$. A normal of slope $-\dfrac{1}{2}$ has $t=\dfrac{1}{2}$: $y=-\dfrac{1}{2}x+4+\dfrac{1}{2}=-\dfrac{1}{2}x+\dfrac{9}{2}$, which is exactly the line above. So $P=(4t^{2},8t)=(1,4)$.

The normal at $t$ meets the parabola again at the parameter $t'$ with $t+t'=-\dfrac{2}{t}$ (from the chord $PQ$ having slope $\dfrac{2}{t+t'}=-t$): $t'=-\dfrac{1}{2}-4=-\dfrac{9}{2}$, so $Q=\left(4\cdot\dfrac{81}{4},\,8\cdot\left(-\dfrac{9}{2}\right)\right)=(81,-36)$.
originality_note: New: the normal at the inflection point of a cubic coincides with a normal of a parabola, which is identified by its slope and then followed to its second intersection (way 5, the link is that a line of slope -t is a normal of the parabola only at parameter t). Closest known: 'normal at t meets the parabola again at -t - 2/t' (a listed skeleton, used here only as a step) and 'normal to a curve at a given point' exercises. Different because: the line comes from a cubic's inflection, and the student must recognise it as a normal of the parabola before using the meet-again relation.

concept_use.Normal to the parabola: point, slope and: The parametric normal y = -tx + 8t + 4t^3 of y^2 = 16x is matched with the line (t = 1/2) and its second intersection uses t' = -t - 2/t.
concept_use.Equation of a normal to a curve: The normal to y = x^3 + 3x^2 + 5x + 8 at its inflection point (-1, 5) is written from y'(-1) = 2.

stem_review: Read as a student: every curve and point is defined before use, every condition is stated, each sentence has one reading; the answer was recomputed with sympy and checked by an independent numerical route, is unique and matches the Answer Plan; no hyperbolic functions or asymptotes. Checked that C has exactly one point of inflection, that the line x + 2y = 9 is a normal of the parabola only at P(1, 4) and meets it at exactly one other point, Q(81, -36), and that 180 is a positive three-digit integer as planned. Changed: No change.
key_step: Recognising the inflection normal as the parabola's normal at t = 1/2 and following it to t' = -9/2.
justification: A chain of several standard stages across two chapters (inflection point, normal to a curve, identification as a parabola normal, meet-again point, area) with no options. More than the single-step normal anchor 2023-P1-Q7 (L2), below the non-routine normal question 2024-P2-Q12 (L4).
